One-factor CFA fit and loadings against a simulated reference

Source: R/cfa_cutoff.R
RMdimCFA.Rd

Fits a one-factor CFA for ordinal items to data and compares its fit indices and the standardized loading of each item with the simulations from RMdimCFACutoff(). Returns two tables, fit indices and loadings, each with the observed value, the simulated reference and a flag.

Usage

RMdimCFA(
  data,
  cutoff,
  p_value = FALSE,
  correction = c("fwer", "fdr_bh", "fdr_by", "none"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  output = c("kable", "dataframe")
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0, the same items as in the simulation. Only complete cases are used.

cutoff

The result of RMdimCFACutoff(). Required, since the observed fit indices cannot be judged without it.

p_value

Logical. Add bootstrap p-values from the simulations and flag on them instead of on the percentile cutoffs. The p-values are one-sided in the unfavourable direction for the fit indices (CFI low, RMSEA and SRMR high) and two-sided for the loadings. The fit indices and the loadings are corrected as two separate families. Default FALSE, which flags at the percentile cutoffs of RMdimCFACutoff() (99 by default). This differs from RMitemInfit(), RMitemRestscore() and RMlocdepQ3(), which use p-values whenever they get the full cutoff object. Here the percentile is chosen when the simulations are run, and the default keeps it as the decision rule.

correction

Character. Correction of the p-values: "fwer" (default, Westfall-Young step-down), "fdr_bh" (Benjamini-Hochberg), "fdr_by" (Benjamini-Yekutieli) or "none". Used only with p_value = TRUE.

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1). A comparison is flagged when its corrected p-value is below alpha. Default 0.05. Used only with p_value = TRUE.

output

Character. "kable" (default) returns each table as a knitr::kable(), "dataframe" as a data.frame.

Value

A named list with fit and loadings, each a knitr_kable or a data.frame by output:

fit

CFI, RMSEA and SRMR with the columns Index, Observed, Cutoff, Direction and Flagged (one-sided, in the unfavourable direction). With p_value = TRUE, also p and padj, and Flagged marks padj < alpha. Flagged is logical. An index lavaan could not compute for data has Observed = NA and Flagged = NA (shown as "not tested" in the kable).

loadings

One row per item with the columns Item, Observed, Expected_low, Expected_high and Flagged ("below", "above" or ""). With p_value = TRUE, also p_loading and padj_loading, and Flagged marks padj_loading < alpha, with the direction from the deviation from the simulated mean.

Details

Bootstrap p-values. The statistic for each comparison is the deviation from the mean of the observed and simulated values together, divided by their SD. The uncorrected p is (1 + count) / (B + 1) for B simulated datasets, so it can be no smaller than 1 / (B + 1). correction = "fwer" uses the Westfall-Young step-down on the studentised maximum, which uses the dependence between the statistics (Westfall & Young, 1993; Ferreira, 2024). It controls the family-wise error rate at any number of iterations, but small p-values are imprecise and decisions depend on the seed when there are few simulations. Use at least 1000 iterations in RMdimCFACutoff(). A warning says so below that. The p-values depend on the model and the sample size, and are reported with the simulated ranges, not instead of them.

Multiple comparisons

The uncorrected p-value controls the error rate of a single comparison. For one item (or item pair) chosen in advance it is the relevant value. Flagging whichever of k comparisons fall below alpha tests k hypotheses at once, and the chance of at least one false flag rises to about \(1 - (1 - \alpha)^k\), for example 34% for k = 8 at alpha = 0.05, even when every uncorrected p-value is calibrated. The corrected p-value controls this. correction = "fwer" bounds the probability of any false flag (strict, less power), and "fdr_bh" and "fdr_by" bound the expected share of false flags among those raised. Use the uncorrected p-value for a single comparison chosen in advance, and a corrected one when screening the whole table, which is the usual case.

References

Ferreira, J. A. (2024). Methods of testing a 'small' or 'moderate' number of hypotheses simultaneously. Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice, 19(1), 6. doi:10.1007/s42519-024-00412-4

Westfall, P. H., & Young, S. S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing. Wiley.

See also

RMdimCFACutoff() for the simulations, RMdimCFAPlot() for the figures.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("eRm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("raschdat1", package = "eRm")
  sim <- RMdimCFACutoff(raschdat1[, 1:8], iterations = 50,
                        parallel = FALSE, seed = 1)
  tabs <- RMdimCFA(raschdat1[, 1:8], cutoff = sim)
  tabs$fit
  tabs$loadings

  # Bootstrap p-values with family-wise (Westfall-Young) correction
  # (use iterations >= 1000 in real analyses for stable p-values)
  RMdimCFA(raschdat1[, 1:8], cutoff = sim, p_value = TRUE)
}
#> Warning: Bootstrap p-values are based on only 50 simulation iterations. With few iterations small p-values are imprecise and decisions depend on the seed; use iterations >= 1000 in RMdimCFACutoff() for reliable p-values.
